text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan unconditionally agrees to implement National Security Council (MGK) measures to cut Islamist activism.
- Islamist-led government gives civil servants 20 to 40 percent pay rise backdated to January.
- Former prime minister Bulent Ecevit drops opposition to uniting his party with a rival left-wing grouping.
- Interior minister gearing up to implement the ban on Islamic dress in the Islamist Fatih district of Istanbul.
- Former national police chief received the power to bug anyone's phone in an unpublicised court order.
- Opposition deputies boycott meeting of parliamentary probe into security scandal.
- International credit rating agency Moody's downgraded Turkey's long-term foreign currency soveregin ceiling note from BA3 to B1.
- Emergency rule governor says the southeast is ready for the Kurdish new year Newroz celebrations and that precautions will be taken to prevent any incident.
